rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Reduce series groups and parallel groups in the order the drawing allows, then find the source current from the final equivalent. Branch currents come from working backward, and the sum of I^2 R should match the source power.

rows.text:
Governing equation for "Series and parallel combination of resistors" — state with units, then use in one numerical.
R_series = Σ R
1/R_parallel = Σ (1/R)

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Equal resistors in parallel divide the current equally.  ·  A wire has nearly zero resistance in these problems.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: A combination problem begins with a sketch of which resistors share a current and which share a node. Two resistors with no branch between them are in series even if the drawing is bent.  ·  Replace each obvious series pair by one resistor, and each obvious parallel pair by one resistor, and redraw. The equivalent of the whole network is the last remaining resistor.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Draw the current splits.  ·  Series first if they share a wire with no branch.  ·  Then parallel.  ·  Power adds once the currents are known.

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: A 6.0 Ω resistor is in series with a parallel pair of 6.0 Ω and 3.0 Ω. The source is 12 V. Find the source current.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: The source current is the source voltage divided by that equivalent. Then work backward. A series resistor carries the current of its string. A parallel branch takes V/R of that branch.  ·  Power in each resistor is I^2 R using the current that actually flows through it. The powers add to the power leaving the source, V I, if the resistors are the only loads.  ·  Three equal resistors can be all in series, all in parallel, or two in parallel with the third in series. Those three arrangements give 3R, R/3 and (3/2)R or a similar result depending on the drawing. The drawing decides.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: A bent wire does not stop two resistors from being in series.  ·  Do not use the parallel formula on a series pair.  ·  Power is not V^2/R using the source voltage on a resistor that does not have the full source voltage.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: A shorted resistor is not a zero-ohm addition in series. It is bypassed.  ·  Name the group you are reducing.  ·  A parallel answer smaller than the branches is a sanity check.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Write R_series = Σ R and say what each symbol means.  ·  Mark the known values, then substitute one step at a time.  ·  Finish with the number, the unit, and the direction when the quantity has one.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: State the limit / condition where a formula or rule stops being valid before applying it.  ·  A resistor that is shorted by a wire has zero voltage and carries no current.
